html:
SMTO-BOOT-0031 — No vLLM build fits this computer's driver and system

GUID: 742d0c6d-cfed-46eb-9d90-cb314402e88b
Slug: boot-vllm-wheel-unavailable
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer checked every ready-made package in the newest vLLM release, and none fits this computer. This happens when the NVIDIA driver is older than those packages need, or the system isn't one they were built for.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Compare the numbers in the message: the CUDA level your driver supports and the published CUDA builds. If every published build is higher, update the NVIDIA driver. Each vLLM build needs a driver that supports at least its CUDA level. The newest cards (compute level 10 or higher) also need a build of 12.8 or newer.
  2. After updating, restart the computer if the driver asks, then run nvidia-smi and check that its "CUDA Version" is at least the lowest published build. nvidia-smi shows the highest CUDA level the driver supports, which is the number the installer compares.
  3. If the message says "none for this Python/OS", the release has no package for this Linux system; use a newer supported Linux system instead. Updating the driver can't help when no package was built for this system at all.
  4. Before installing again, run conda env list. If the environment name from this attempt is listed, use a new name or remove that half-built environment first. The package search happens after the environment is created, and the installer won't install into a name that already exists.

What success looks like

  • The installer prints "Selected vLLM" with a version and CUDA backend, then continues installing.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0031 line with the version and CUDA numbers, and send it to the person who manages this computer. Don't install an older vLLM or a different build by hand; the installer doesn't choose older releases, and a mismatched build may not run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • select_wheel found no wheel for the latest vLLM release that matches this interpreter's platform tags, has a CUDA build at or below the driver's supported CUDA level, and meets the CUDA 12.8 floor for SM 10.x and newer GPUs.

What this means

  • Filtering published release wheels by package/version/tags, architecture, GPU generation and driver CUDA level leaves no compatible candidates. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Filtering published release wheels by package/version/tags, architecture, GPU generation and driver CUDA level leaves no compatible candidates.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare supported Python/OS tags, driver level and every selected GPU with the reported available builds.

How to fix it

  • Compare the driver CUDA level with the published CUDA builds listed in the message: upgrade the NVIDIA driver if every build is higher (with an SM 10.x or newer GPU, only builds at CUDA 12.8 or above qualify), or use an upstream-supported OS, glibc and Python if the list reads 'none for this Python/OS'. No older release is selected automatically; remove the partial environment or use a new name before reinstalling.
  • Use an upstream-supported host/Python/build or update the NVIDIA driver where needed. No older release is selected automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A verified published candidate matches the intended environment without automatic downgrade guessing.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
